In dynamic ftrace
column2: the mcount function starts off pointing to a stub

column1: function that just returns.
On start up
column2: the call to the stub is modified to point to a ""record_ip""

column1: function. The job of the record_ip function is to add the function to
a pre-allocated hash list. If the function is already there
ignored
column2: otherwise it is added to the list.

column1: Later
column2: a ftraced daemon wakes up and calls kstop_machine if any functions

column1: have been recorded
column2: and changes the calls to the recorded functions to

column1: a simple nop.  If no functions were recorded
column2: the daemon goes back to sleep.

column1: The daemon wakes up once a second to see if it needs to update any newly
recorded functions into nops.  Usually it does not
column2: but if a lot of code

column1: has been executed for the first time in the kernel
will call kstop_machine to update those into nops.
The problem currently is that there's no way to stop the daemon from doing
this
column2: and it can cause unneeded latencies (800us which for some is bothersome).

column1: This patch adds a new file /debugfs/tracing/ftraced_enabled. If the daemon
is active
column2: reading this will return ""enabled\n"" and ""disabled\n"" when the

column1: daemon is not running. To disable the daemon
disable"" into this file
column2: and ""1"" or ""enable"" to re-enable the daemon.

column1: Since the daemon is used to convert the functions into nops to increase
the performance of the system
column2: I also added that anytime something is

column1: written into the ftraced_enabled file
are new functions that have been detected that need to be converted.
This way the user can disable the daemon but still be able to control the
conversion of the mcount calls to nops by simply
""echo 0 > /debugfs/tracing/ftraced_enabled""
when they need to do more conversions.
To see the number of converted functions:
""cat /debugfs/tracing/dyn_ftrace_total_info""
